newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies following the decline of the dollar abroad, dealers said.

"The session opened with a strong rise of the shekel following the weakening of the dollar against the mark. Later, when the central bank announced the lowering of the interest rate the trend did not change," said Zahi Elias at Bank Leumi.
Earlier on Monday the Bank of Israel said it was lowering its key lending rate to commercial banks for September by 0.5 percentage point to an annualised 15.8 percent.
"The market expected a higher cut and the shekel continues to rise. The basket is already 6.9 percent below the slope," he said.
The shekel can fluctuate in a trading band of 7.0 percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the market believes the central bank would intervene by buying foreign currency.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1410 against 3.1550 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5402 shekels against 3.5471 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9110 shekels per 100 yen against 2.9109 on Friday and against the mark at 2.1244 shekels per mark against 2.1170 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1400 shekels.
